Target audience: High school students interested in computer science and mathematics

Section: section_1 — Introduction: The Binary Basics (1 minute)

Lecture lines:
Binary represents numbers using switches, ON or OFF.
Each switch corresponds to a power of two.
Thirteen is eight plus four plus one.
This equals one-one-zero-one in binary.
Any decimal number uniquely sums these powers.

Planned animations:
Create a neon-green (#00FF00) circle representing a bit.
Move the bit circle to the center of the screen.
Flash the bit circle in bright yellow (#FFFF00) to signal activity.

Section: section_2 — Mapping Towers of Hanoi to Binary (1.5 minutes)

Lecture lines:
Moving N disks requires two to the N minus one moves.
Seven moves are needed for three disks.
Sequence counts binary like a rhythmic clock.

Planned animations:
Draw three vertical stacks of varying sizes (#FF0000).
Place a numeric binary label (#00FFFF) beside each stack.
Animate the stacks transforming into a binary sequence (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_3 — Visualizing the Algorithm (1.5 minutes)

Lecture lines:
Binary patterns dictate exactly which disk moves next.
Bit the Bot moves Disk One on odd steps.
Bit the Bot moves Disk Two on steps two, six.
Bit the Bot moves Disk Three on step four.
Movement follows the least significant changing bit.

Planned animations:
Visualize a recursive flow arrow (#00FF00) moving between disks.
Highlight the smallest disk in bright cyan (#00FFFF).
Shift the disks using a smooth translation animation (#FFFFFF).

Section: section_4 — Synthesis and Application (1 minute)

Lecture lines:
Binary is an instruction set for recursive puzzles.
Logical pulse controls every disk transition.
This rhythm scales to any number of disks.

Planned animations:
Display a combined binary tree (#FFFFFF) on screen.
Highlight the root node in bright magenta (#FF00FF).
Animate the nodes fading into a final summary diagram.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
